Canonical rail spacing and route-aware contextual blurb layer

research_objects.result: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN unavailable to GitHub Actions; production remained unchanged

ctc_tags.rationale: The human observed that committed repository state and experienced public state diverged; the observation materially changed the implementation path.

ctc_tags.domain: Technology as Tool to Think With
ctc_tags.rationale: The interface now exposes page-specific contextual meaning consistently instead of leaving navigation as undifferentiated controls.
A failed deployment exposed an infrastructural assumption and generated a revised deployment design rather than being hidden.
The build-in-public environment requires repository work to become visible public state; deployment is part of the collaboration boundary.

ontology_tags.rationale: Human observation returned the artifact to revision: commit -> experience -> notice stale state -> diagnose -> revise infrastructure.
A persistent environment requires a reproducible bridge between repository state and the running public system.
The failure demonstrates the need to distinguish committed source state, tested state, deployed state, and experienced public state rather than collapsing them into one claim of completion.

uncaptured_observations.observation: Build-in-public has at least four distinguishable states: authored/committed, mechanically tested, deployed, and publicly experienced. Treating these as one state creates false claims of completion.
uncaptured_observations.reason_unmapped: This appears to be a cross-cutting provenance and research-method principle rather than clearly one of the seven learner-facing CTC domains.
